Maintenance Report — MNT-0111-005

Asset: WELL-0111 (NE-07 Well 111, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 16 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 16 Jun 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0111-0034 on 2023-06-15 Report written: 18 Jun 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0111-0034 at 11:45 on 2023-06-15 found crude oil on the pad: about 1.8% of the pad area, estimated 0.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 386 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 309 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.6 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0111-005 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.58% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0111-020

Asset: WELL-0111 (NE-07 Well 111, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 06 Jun 2025 08:00 · Finished: 25 Jun 2025 06:00 · Well stopped for this job: 454 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0111-0132 on 2025-06-05 Report written: 01 Jul 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0111-0132 showed the wellhead at 29.6 °C with the air at 28.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 17 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 386 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 309 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0111-020 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0111-023

Asset: WELL-0111 (NE-07 Well 111, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 04 Oct 2025 08:00 · Finished: 12 Nov 2025 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 938 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0111-0149 on 2025-10-02 Report written: 12 Nov 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0111-0149 showed the wellhead at 31.4 °C with the air at 26.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 37 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0111-028

Asset: WELL-0111 (NE-07 Well 111, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 19 Jun 2026 08:00 · Finished: 30 Jun 2026 06:00 · Well stopped for this job: 262 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0111-0186 on 2026-06-18 Report written: 01 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0111-0186 showed the wellhead at 34.9 °C with the air at 31.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
